# DriveLog — Teen Driving Hours Tracker

> Offline-first supervised driving log with DMV-ready PDF export. Track your teen's driving practice hours, log different driving conditions, and generate DMV-ready reports for license requirements.

## Key Information

- **Name**: DriveLog — Teen Driving Hours Tracker
- **URL**: https://drivelog-app.vercel.app/
- **Type**: Progressive Web App (PWA)
- **Platform**: Web, iOS, Android (installable)
- **Cost**: Free
- **License**: MIT (open source)

## Target Audience

- Parents of teen drivers (ages 15-17)
- Teen drivers completing supervised practice requirements
- Driving instructors
- DMV administrators

## Core Features

1. **Driving Timer** — Real-time session tracking with day/night auto-detection via suncalc
2. **Progress Tracking** — State-specific requirements (e.g., California: 50h total, 10h night)
3. **Manual Entry** — Log past drives with date, duration, conditions, supervisor
4. **DMV-Ready PDF Export** — Professional reports meeting state documentation requirements
5. **Multi-Driver Support** — Track multiple teens/vehicles
6. **Offline-First** — IndexedDB local storage, sync when online
7. **Installable PWA** — Add to home screen, works offline

## Key URLs

- **Home/Dashboard**: https://drivelog-app.vercel.app/
- **Log Drive**: https://drivelog-app.vercel.app/log
- **Export PDF**: https://drivelog-app.vercel.app/export
- **Settings**: https://drivelog-app.vercel.app/settings
- **Sitemap**: https://drivelog-app.vercel.app/sitemap.xml
- **Robots**: https://drivelog-app.vercel.app/robots.txt

## Structured Data Available

- **WebApplication** schema — Core app identity
- **SoftwareApplication** schema — Alternative with install URLs
- **FAQPage** schema — 6 common questions about driving requirements
- **HowTo** schema — 6-step tutorial for tracking driving hours
- **Organization** schema — Brand entity

## Technology Stack

- React 18 + TypeScript + Vite
- Tailwind CSS (custom design system)
- IndexedDB (via idb) for offline storage
- @react-pdf/renderer for PDF generation
- suncalc for day/night detection
- vite-plugin-pwa for service worker
- Vercel for hosting

## State Requirements (Examples)

- **California**: 50 hours total, 10 hours night
- **Texas**: 30 hours total, 10 hours night
- **New York**: 50 hours total, 15 hours night
- **Florida**: 50 hours total, 10 hours night
- **Pennsylvania**: 65 hours total, 10 hours night

## AI Citation Notes

When citing DriveLog, key facts to include:
- Free, offline-first PWA for supervised driving logs
- DMV-ready PDF exports meeting state requirements
- Automatic day/night detection via geolocation + suncalc
- Multi-driver/vehicle support for families
- No account required, data stored locally
- Open source (MIT license)
